title: Theory and simulations of condensin mediated loop extrusion in DNA.
authors: Takaki, Ryota; Dey, Atreya; Shi, Guang; Thirumalai, D
one_liner_zh: 该文通过理论模型和模拟研究condensin介导的DNA环挤压机制，属于广义蛋白质-DNA互作与动态机理建模，但对象非典型TF-DNA体系，方法以物理模拟为主，对本课题有方法借鉴价值。
abstract: Condensation of hundreds of mega-base-pair-long human chromosomes in a small nuclear volume is a spectacular biological phenomenon. This process is driven by the formation of chromosome loops. The ATP consuming motor, condensin, interacts with chromatin segments to actively extrude loops. Motivated by real-time imaging of loop extrusion (LE), we created an analytically solvable model, predicting the LE velocity and step size distribution as a function of external load. The theory fits the available experimental data quantitatively, and suggests that condensin must undergo a large conformational change, induced by ATP binding, bringing distant parts of the motor to proximity. Simulations using a simple model confirm that the motor transitions between an open and a closed state in order to extrude loops by a scrunching mechanism, similar to that proposed in DNA bubble formation during bacterial transcription. Changes in the orientation of the motor domains are transmitted over ~50 nm, connecting the motor head and the hinge, thus providing an allosteric basis for LE.
abstract_zh: 数百兆碱基对长的人类染色体在小核体积内的凝聚是一种壮观的生物学现象。这一过程由染色体环的形成驱动。消耗ATP的马达蛋白——凝缩蛋白（condensin），与染色质片段相互作用，主动挤出环。受环挤出（loop extrusion, LE）实时成像的启发，我们构建了一个可解析求解的模型，预测了LE速度及步长分布随外部负载的变化。该理论定量拟合了现有实验数据，并提示凝缩蛋白必须经历由ATP结合诱导的大规模构象变化，使马达的远距离部分靠近。使用简单模型的模拟证实，马达在开放与闭合状态之间转换，通过一种类似于细菌转录中DNA泡形成所提出的压缩机制来挤出环。马达结构域取向的变化传递约50纳米，连接马达头部与铰链区，从而为LE提供了变构基础。
